stances.claim: Morales's dismissal of the GMA fertilizer-scam graft charges is anchored on the utter lack of evidence showing GMA's criminal complicity -- complainant failed to present any documentary or testimonial evidence proving GMA's knowledge of, or participation in, the scheme perpetrated by Lorenzo and Bolante; all documents submitted were prepared and signed by other persons.
stances.confidence: asserted on direct review of resolution

stances.claim: Command responsibility cannot ground criminal liability for GMA because, per Rubrico v. Arroyo (Feb 18 2010), no Philippine law provides for criminal liability under the doctrine of command responsibility -- and qualified political agency cannot extend either, per Reyes v. Rural Bank of San Miguel (Feb 27 2004), without proof of actual authorization.

Being the mere superior of officials who committed wrongdoing, by itself and nothing else, is not sufficient proof of criminal complicity -- as illustrated by President Marcos not being indicted for the Ninoy Aquino murder despite being the superior of the soldiers and officers charged and found guilty.
stances.rhetorical_move: Marcos-Ninoy parallel as canonical superior-not-mastermind precedent

stances.claim: That GMA has been publicly maligned for the many controversies that plagued her reign is no reason to deny her the basic rights of every citizen -- and Morales's overall record (also filing PCSO plunder and NBN/ZTE graft against GMA) shows fairness and objectivity, ruling for or against GMA as the evidence and law demand.
stances.confidence: asserted as defense of due process and prosecutorial integrity

notable_anecdotes: The Marcos-not-indicted-for-Ninoy-murder parallel -- 'that heinous crime committed in broad daylight in a very public place remains a mystery to this date' -- extraordinary doctrinal-historical analogy used to defend Morales's GMA-fertilizer-dismissal by invoking the most politically sensitive unsolved-mystery in PH 20th-century history.

Direct review of the OOO resolution by CJP -- 'I myself was surprised. So, I secured a copy of and reviewed the dismissal resolution' -- a rare disclosure of independent verification of a primary document before opining.
The 121-of-179-recipients-from-LAKAS-CMD detail -- Arroyo's own party as 67% of fertilizer-fund beneficiaries -- flagged as suspicious but legally insufficient without proof of GMA's knowledge.
Morales's fairness record -- dismissing this graft but filing PCSO funds plunder and NBN/ZTE graft against GMA -- used as the counterweight that defuses partisan-favoritism accusations.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban defends Ombudsman Conchita Carpio Morales's dismissal of graft charges against former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo in connection with the P728M fertilizer fund scam against the backlash captured in the May 14 Inquirer editorial Where will the buck stop? He secured a copy of the dismissal resolution (prepared by a three-person panel chaired by Deputy Ombudsman Gerard A. Mosquera, approved by Morales) and reviewed it directly. The facts narrated are sparse: then-Agriculture Sec Luis Lorenzo authorized Undersecretary Jocelyn Joc-Joc Bolante to distribute the fund, which went to LGUs and legislative districts not farm zones (179 proponents, of which 121 were LAKAS-CMD members -- Arroyo's own party). Three issues were raised: Anti-Graft Sec 3(c) violation, criminal liability under command responsibility, and qualified political agency. On the first, the OOO held that complainant failed to present any documentary or testimonial evidence proving GMA's knowledge of, or participation in, the scheme -- all documents were prepared and signed by other persons. On the second, citing Rubrico v. Arroyo (Feb 18 2010), no Philippine law provides for criminal liability under the doctrine of command responsibility. On the third, citing Reyes v. Rural Bank of San Miguel (Feb 27 2004), qualified political agency cannot extend without proof of actual authorization. Panganiban's assessment: the resolution is anchored on the utter lack of evidence -- and being a mere superior, by itself and nothing else, is insufficient, as illustrated by President Marcos not being indicted for the Ninoy Aquino murder despite being the soldiers' superior (a heinous crime committed in broad daylight in a very public place that remains a mystery to this date). He invokes Salonga v. Pano (Feb 18 1985) -- PI purpose is to secure the innocent against hasty, malicious, oppressive prosecution and protect the state from useless and expensive trials -- and closes by defending Morales's overall fairness, citing her parallel filings of PCSO funds plunder and NBN/ZTE graft cases against GMA: these decisions show her fairness and objectivity in performing her work, ruling for or against GMA as the evidence and law demand.
